scope: Training diagnostic only. Take every non-adversarial LoCoMo question on the six training histories whose evidence is nonempty, fully resolved and crosses at least two disjoint session pairs (1-2, 3-4, ...). Assign each original question exactly once, to the last session containing its evidence. Do not read validation or test answers.
intervention: Process every session from 1 through the assigned endpoint in temporal order, including sessions without annotated evidence. Commit the background skill bit for each dialogue and session from the low bit of the first SHA-256 byte of memskill-cross-window-v1/dialogue/session. At the endpoint execute both temporal and activity in the same slot of the same top-three selection. Require identical preceding actions, memory writes, retrievals and pre-action states. Use the same BF16 reader, GPU encoder and token F1. The endpoint is an evidence-defined training intervention. It estimates a local effect at first availability, not full-history deployment value.
order: Order by endpoint session number, then put histories excluded from the two-history pilot first, then dialogue ID. Generate all eligible endpoints independent of prior scores. Keep a held-four-histories summary for the frozen strength/rank pilots and separate pooled or in-fit results. Numerical pilot parameters must already exist when the cohort is locked. No additional selection credit is created by an unverified end-to-end difference.
evaluation: Report both branch scores and matched expected focal F1, with native, terminal, both fixed skills, both frozen pilots, fixed maximum strength, source-usage matched and prefix-only controls. Retain greedy alternatives, probabilities, ordered skill choices, per-question evidence distances and usage. Report breakdown by original category, dialogue, prefix length and gap. The independent development and two locked full-history tests continue to govern promotion.
